target_customer: Ecommerce merchants (initially Shopify stores and social sellers in Africa) that pay for voice and AI sales agents and agent-ready storefronts
problem: Merchants lose sales because shoppers cannot easily browse and buy by talking in local languages, and merchant catalogs are not accessible to external shopping agents.
business_model: SaaS subscription with a free tier, a 15 USD per month Premium plan and custom pricing, per the company site
product_category: AI voice commerce agents and agent-ready ecommerce infrastructure

founders.name: Felix Manford
previous_startups: Tendo, social reselling platform (the earlier name of this company)
founders.background_notes: YC bio also uses the spelling Teno.

founders.name: Evans Darbo Boateng
founders.background_notes: Profile lists software engineer with 6+ years of experience; no employers or education found.

competitors.name: Paystack Commerce
competitors.what: Social commerce storefront product from a payments company, launched June 2020

competitors.name: Flutterwave Store
competitors.what: Social commerce product from Flutterwave, launched May 2020

technical_complexity.rationale: Social reselling needed catalog, ordering and payments in Ghana in 2021; the current voice agent in 50+ languages adds speech and LLM work, but that came after the batch.

defensibility.rationale: Storefront and reselling tools were copyable by payments firms and Shopify; the moat would be merchant integrations and local language support.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Payment companies launched social commerce products in 2020; no acquisition of this company was found.

market_need_then: Catalyst Fund's January 2022 note frames demand around informal digital sellers in Ghana and the fact that WhatsApp and Facebook were adding commerce features.

branding.domain_note: Site is dukesell.com; the free plan badge says Made with DukeQ, unexplained.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct voice-first pitch: Let customers shop by talking, Sell while you sleep

rebrands.why: Not stated; inferred from the YC page for Tendo resolving to Dukesell with Tendo named in the founder bios

brand_strength.rationale: No independent press on the brand found; searches for Dukesell returned nothing specific.

pivots.from: Tendo, social reselling platform in Ghana
pivots.to: Duke, voice and agent-ready commerce for merchants

outcome_analysis: The company began as Tendo, a Ghana social reselling platform, joined YC in Winter 2022, and later renamed and repositioned as Dukesell around AI voice agents and agentic commerce. It remains active with about 15 people. Public funding evidence is thin, the pivot date is unknown, and the outcome is still open, so no success or failure judgement is made beyond survival.
notes: Identity link: the YC page for the slug tendo shows the Dukesell record, and founder bios say Tendo, so the company was formerly Tendo (rename inferred, not stated). Aggregators (Startuplist, Seedtable, CB Insights) report YC pre-seed or seed around January 2022, a July 2021 pre-seed, a 25K grant from Morgan Stanley Inclusive Ventures Lab in September 2024 and a 1.25M seed in April 2025 from Renew Capital among others; totals conflict by a factor of ten, all unverified. YC page says founded 2022 while aggregators say Tendo started in 2021. Competitor article was seen as a search result, not opened. Education and employers not found.
